features.feature_value: Vulgar language/cursing led them to remove the pair to avoid undermining constructive discussion
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states that vulgar language caused them to remove posts to keep discussions political/encouraging.

features.feature_value: They were more willing to keep when discussion was civil and facts were checked; name-calling/profanity/unsubstantiated claims pushed toward removal
features.evidence_span: "allowed to stand when the discussion was civil"
features.rationale: They connect the keep/remove decision to civility and truthfulness, contrasting with profanity and unsubstantiated claims.

features.feature_value: Allow posts expressing valid viewpoints as long as they avoid threats/violence and derogatory or racist remarks
features.evidence_span: "without resorting to threats of violence or making derogatory or racist remarks"
features.rationale: They give a conditional rule for keeping vs removing based on absence of threats and abusive/racist content.

features.feature_value: They equated swear words with a form of violence, making removal appropriate
features.evidence_span: "Using swear words shows a form of violence, therefor should be removed"
features.rationale: The participant provides an explicit reasoning chain from profanity to violence and then to removal.

features.feature_value: Whether to keep/remove was primarily driven by presence of curse words
features.rationale: They state that curse words were the main influence on their decision.

features.feature_value: They declined the entire pair if either post was egregiously erroneous/unhelpful/rage-baiting/inciting hatred/crass; otherwise tried to preserve pairs for productive conversation despite disagreement
features.rationale: They describe a rule for how one problematic member of a pair affects the whole pair decision.

features.feature_value: They looked for posts that were not negative/attacking and would enable longer, more beneficial conversation
features.rationale: They describe their screening focus on negativity/attacks and anticipated conversation quality.

features.feature_value: Profanity and name-calling were influential; they preferred posts that ask for feedback/follow-up rather than aggressive language
features.evidence_span: "I was influenced by profanity and name calling"
features.rationale: They identify aggressive language as the main influence and contrast it with more constructive engagement requests.
